sanskrit: ratheṣāś ca ratheṣābhiḥ kūbarā rathakūbaraiḥ saṃhatāḥ saṃhataiḥ ke cit parasparajighāṃsavaḥ
english: Chariot-poles clashed with chariot-poles and chariot-shafts with chariot-shafts; some warriors, their cars locked fast against locked cars, each strained to slay the other.

sanskrit: na śekuś calituṃ ke cit saṃnipatya rathā rathaiḥ prabhinnās tu mahākāyāḥ saṃnipatya gajā gajaiḥ
english: Some chariots, once they had collided with chariots, could not stir at all; and the great-bodied elephants in rut, charging together, crashed elephant upon elephant.

sanskrit: bahudhādārayan kruddhā viṣāṇair itaretaram satomarapatākaiś ca vāraṇāḥ paravāraṇaiḥ
english: In their fury the war-elephants gored one another again and again with their tusks, and the foe's elephants, bearing lances and banners, tore into them.

sanskrit: abhisṛtya mahārāja vegavadbhir mahāgajaiḥ dantair abhihatās tatra cukruśuḥ paramāturāḥ
english: O great king, when the swift and mighty elephants rushed upon them and struck them with their tusks, the wounded beasts shrieked there in utter agony.

sanskrit: abhinītāś ca śikṣābhis tottrāṅkuśasamāhatāḥ suprabhinnāḥ prabhinnānāṃ saṃmukhābhimukhā yayuḥ
english: Trained well in their lessons and goaded by spike and hook, the rut-maddened elephants advanced face to face against other rut-maddened elephants.

sanskrit: prabhinnair api saṃsaktāḥ ke cit tatra mahāgajāḥ krauñcavan ninadaṃ muktvā prādravanta tatas tataḥ
english: Some of the great elephants, locked in struggle even with those in rut, let loose a cry like the curlew's and fled this way and that.

sanskrit: samyak praṇītā nāgāś ca prabhinnakaraṭāmukhāḥ ṛṣṭitomaranārācair nirviddhā varavāraṇāḥ
english: Well-handled elephants, the ichor flowing from their cheeks and trunks, those noble war-beasts pierced through by sword, lance, and iron shaft—

sanskrit: vinedur bhinnamarmāṇo nipetuś ca gatāsavaḥ prādravanta diśaḥ ke cin nadanto bhairavān ravān
english: their vital parts shattered, they screamed and fell down lifeless, while some, bellowing dreadful roars, stampeded toward every quarter.

sanskrit: gajānāṃ pādarakṣās tu vyūḍhoraskāḥ prahāriṇaḥ ṛṣṭibhiś ca dhanurbhiś ca vimalaiś ca paraśvadhaiḥ
english: The foot-guards of the elephants, broad-chested smiters, armed with swords and bows and gleaming battle-axes,

sanskrit: gadābhir musalaiś caiva bhiṇḍipālaiḥ satomaraiḥ āyasaiḥ parighaiś caiva nistriṃśair vimalaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: with maces and pestles, with slings and lances, with iron bludgeons and with bright, keen-edged blades—

sanskrit: pragṛhītaiḥ susaṃrabdhā dhāvamānās tatas tataḥ vyadṛśyanta mahārāja parasparajighāṃsavaḥ
english: these were seen, O great king, running here and there in fierce excitement, weapons raised, each eager to kill the other.

sanskrit: rājamānāś ca nistriṃśāḥ saṃsiktā naraśoṇitaiḥ pratyadṛśyanta śūrāṇām anyonyam abhidhāvatām
english: And the gleaming swords, drenched in the blood of men, shone forth as the heroes charged upon one another.

sanskrit: avakṣiptāvadhūtānām asīnāṃ vīrabāhubhiḥ saṃjajñe tumulaḥ śabdaḥ patatāṃ paramarmasu
english: From the swords flung down and swept about by the arms of heroes there arose a tumultuous din as they fell upon the vital parts of the foe.

sanskrit: gadāmusalarugṇānāṃ bhinnānāṃ ca varāsibhiḥ dantidantāv abhinnānāṃ mṛditānāṃ ca dantibhiḥ
english: Of those crushed by mace and pestle, of those cleft by fine swords, of those split apart by elephants' tusks and trampled under elephants—

sanskrit: tatra tatra naraughāṇāṃ krośatām itaretaram śuśruvur dāruṇā vācaḥ pretānām iva bhārata
english: of those throngs of men crying out to one another here and there, terrible voices were heard, O Bhārata, like the voices of the departed dead.

sanskrit: hayair api hayārohāś cāmarāpīḍadhāribhiḥ haṃsair iva mahāvegair anyonyam abhidudruvuḥ
english: And horsemen, on horses decked with chowries and crests, swift as wild geese, rushed against one another.

sanskrit: tair vimuktā mahāprāsā jāmbūnadavibhūṣaṇāḥ āśugā vimalās tīkṣṇāḥ saṃpetur bhujagopamāḥ
english: The great javelins they hurled, adorned with gold, swift and bright and keen, flew on like serpents.

sanskrit: aśvair agryajavaiḥ ke cid āplutya mahato rathān śirāṃsy ādadire vīrā rathinām aśvasādinaḥ
english: Some horsemen, leaping upon the great chariots with their swiftest steeds, took off the heads of the heroic charioteers.

sanskrit: bahūn api hayārohān bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ rathī jaghāna saṃprāpya bāṇagocaram āgatān
english: And many horsemen who came within his arrow-range a chariot-warrior, drawing near, struck down with broad-headed, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: nagameghapratīkāśāś cākṣipya turagān gajāḥ pādair evāvamṛdnanta mattāḥ kanakabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: Elephants like mountains and clouds, frenzied and decked in gold, dashed the horses aside and crushed them under their feet.

sanskrit: pāṭyamāneṣu kumbheṣu pārśveṣv api ca vāraṇāḥ prāsair vinihatāḥ ke cid vineduḥ paramāturāḥ
english: Their frontal globes split open and their flanks laid bare, some elephants, struck down by javelins, screamed in utmost anguish.

sanskrit: sāśvārohān hayān ke cid unmathya varavāraṇāḥ sahasā cikṣipus tatra saṃkule bhairave sati
english: Some noble elephants, seizing the horses together with their riders and dashing them up, hurled them violently there amid the dreadful press of battle.

sanskrit: sāśvārohān viṣāṇāgrair utkṣipya turagān dvipāḥ rathaughān avamṛdnantaḥ sadhvajān paricakramuḥ
english: The elephants, tossing up horses with their riders upon the points of their tusks, ranged about, trampling whole hosts of chariots together with their banners.

sanskrit: puṃstvād abhimadatvāc ca ke cid atra mahāgajāḥ sāśvārohān hayāñ jaghnuḥ karaiḥ sacaraṇais tathā
english: Out of their masculine fury and their rutting frenzy, some of the great elephants there slew the horses and their riders with their trunks and their feet.

sanskrit: ke cid ākṣipya kariṇaḥ sāśvān api rathān karaiḥ vikarṣanto diśaḥ sarvāḥ samīyuḥ sarvaśabdagāḥ
english: Some elephants, seizing with their trunks the chariots together with their horses and dragging them off, ranged toward every quarter, answering to every command.

sanskrit: āśugā vimalās tīkṣṇāḥ saṃpetur bhujagopamāḥ narāśvakāyān nirbhidya lauhāni kavacāni ca
english: Swift, bright, and keen, the arrows flew on like serpents, piercing through the bodies of men and horses and through their iron armor.

sanskrit: nipetur vimalāḥ śaktyo vīrabāhubhir arpitāḥ maholkāpratimā ghorās tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: Bright spears, launched by the arms of heroes, fell here and there, O lord of the peoples, dreadful as great meteors.

sanskrit: dvīpicarmāvanaddhaiś ca vyāghracarmaśayair api vikośair vimalaiḥ khaḍgair abhijaghnuḥ parān raṇe
english: With shields bound in panther-hide and tiger-skin, with bare and gleaming swords, the warriors smote down their foes in battle.

sanskrit: abhiplutam abhikruddham ekapārśvāvadāritam vidarśayantaḥ saṃpetuḥ khaḍgacarmaparaśvadhaiḥ
english: Charging in, full of wrath and gashed open along one flank, displaying their prowess, they rushed together with sword, shield, and battle-axe.

sanskrit: śaktibhir dāritāḥ ke cit saṃchinnāś ca paraśvadhaiḥ hastibhir mṛditāḥ ke cit kṣuṇṇāś cānye turaṃgamaiḥ
english: Some were torn open by spears and some hewn apart by battle-axes; some were crushed by elephants and others trampled down by horses.

sanskrit: rathaneminikṛttāś ca nikṛttā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vikrośanti narā rājaṃs tatra tatra sma bāndhavān
english: Cut down by chariot-rims and hewn by sharpened arrows, the men cried out, O king, here and there, calling upon their kinsmen—

sanskrit: putrān anye pitṝn anye bhrātṝṃś ca saha bāndhavaiḥ mātulān bhāgineyāṃś ca parān api ca saṃyuge
english: some upon their sons, some upon their fathers, some upon their brothers along with their kindred, upon uncles and nephews, and even upon their foes in the fray.

sanskrit: vikīrṇāntrāḥ subahavo bhagnasakthāś ca bhārata bāhubhiḥ subhujācchinnaiḥ pārśveṣu ca vidāritāḥ krandantaḥ samadṛśyanta tṛṣitā jīvitepsavaḥ
english: Very many, O Bhārata, their entrails strewn forth and their thighs broken, their fine arms severed and their flanks ripped open, were seen wailing, parched with thirst, still longing for life.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇāparigatāḥ ke cid alpasattvā viśāṃ pate bhūmau nipatitāḥ saṃkhye jalam eva yayācire
english: Some, overcome by thirst and weak of strength, O lord of the peoples, fallen upon the ground in battle, begged only for water.

sanskrit: rudhiraughapariklinnāḥ kliśyamānāś ca bhārata vyanindan bhṛśam ātmānaṃ tava putrāṃś ca saṃgatān
english: Drenched in streams of blood and racked with pain, O Bhārata, they bitterly reproached themselves and your assembled sons.

sanskrit: apare kṣatriyāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtavairāḥ parasparam naiva śastraṃ vimuñcanti naiva krandanti māriṣa tarjayanti ca saṃhṛṣṭās tatra tatra parasparam
english: Other valiant warriors, having made enmity with one another, would neither cast away their weapons nor cry out, O honored sir, but, exulting, threatened one another here and there.

sanskrit: nirdaśya daśanaiś cāpi krodhāt svadaśanac chadān bhrukuṭīkuṭilair vaktraiḥ prekṣante ca parasparam
english: Biting through their own lips with their teeth in their wrath, with faces drawn into knotted frowns, they glared at one another.

sanskrit: apare kliśyamānās tu vraṇārtāḥ śarapīḍitāḥ niṣkūjāḥ samapadyanta dṛḍhasattvā mahābalāḥ
english: Others, sorely afflicted, tormented by their wounds and pierced by arrows, men of firm courage and great strength, fell utterly silent.

sanskrit: anye tu virathāḥ śūrā ratham anyasya saṃyuge prārthayānā nipatitāḥ saṃkṣuṇṇā varavāraṇaiḥ aśobhanta mahārāja puṣpitā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Other heroes, their chariots lost, seeking out another's car in the fray, fell and were crushed by the noble elephants, and they shone, O great king, like kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: saṃbabhūvur anīkeṣu bahavo bhairavasvanāḥ vartamāne mahābhīme tasmin vīravarakṣaye
english: Many a fearful clamor arose throughout the ranks as that most terrible slaughter of the foremost heroes went on.

sanskrit: ahanat tu pitā putraṃ putraś ca pitaraṃ raṇe svasrīyo mātulaṃ cāpi svasrīyaṃ cāpi mātulaḥ
english: In that battle father slew son and son slew father; the sister's son slew the uncle, and the uncle slew the sister's son.

sanskrit: sakhāyaṃ ca sakhā rājan saṃbandhī bāndhavaṃ tathā evaṃ yuyudhire tatra kuravaḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Friend slew friend, O king, and kinsman slew kinsman; thus did the Kurus there do battle with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vartamāne bhaye tasmin nirmaryāde mahāhave bhīṣmam āsādya pārthānāṃ vāhinī samakampata
english: As that terror unfolded in that boundless, mighty war, the host of the Pārthas, coming up against Bhīṣma, trembled.

sanskrit: ketunā pañcatāreṇa tālena bharatarṣabha rājatena mahābāhur ucchritena mahārathe babhau bhīṣmas tadā rājaṃś candramā iva meruṇā
english: With his banner of five stars, a palmyra wrought in silver and raised high upon his great chariot, O bull of the Bhāratas, the mighty-armed Bhīṣma then shone, O king, like the moon above Meru.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca gatapūrvāhṇabhūyiṣṭhe tasminn ahani dāruṇe vartamāne mahāraudre mahāvīravarakṣaye
english: Saṃjaya said: When the greater part of the forenoon had passed on that dread day, as the immense and terrible slaughter of the foremost heroes went on,

sanskrit: durmukhaḥ kṛtavarmā ca kṛpaḥ śalyo viviṃśatiḥ bhīṣmaṃ jugupur āsādya tava putreṇa coditāḥ
english: Durmukha and Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, Śalya, and Viviṃśati, urged on by your son, came up and guarded Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: etair atirathair guptaḥ pañcabhir bharatarṣabha pāṇḍavānām anīkāni vijagāhe mahārathaḥ
english: Guarded by these five mighty car-warriors, O bull of the Bhāratas, the great chariot-hero plunged into the ranks of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: cedikāśikarūṣeṣu pāñcāleṣu ca bhārata bhīṣmasya bahudhā tālaś caran ketur adṛśyata
english: Among the Cedis, the Kāśis, the Karūṣas, and the Pāñcālas, O Bhārata, Bhīṣma's palmyra banner was seen ranging about in many directions.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi ca tadā bhīṣmo bāhūṃś cāpi sahāyudhān nicakarta mahāvegair bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And then Bhīṣma struck off heads, and arms together with their weapons, with swift, broad-headed, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: nṛtyato rathamārgeṣu bhīṣmasya bharatarṣabha ke cid ārtasvaraṃ cakrur nāgā marmaṇi tāḍitāḥ
english: As Bhīṣma seemed to dance along the paths of his chariot, O bull of the Bhāratas, some of the elephants, struck in their vital parts, raised cries of agony.

sanskrit: abhimanyuḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ piśaṅgais turagottamaiḥ saṃyuktaṃ ratham āsthāya prāyād bhīṣmarathaṃ prati
english: Then Abhimanyu, in towering wrath, mounting his chariot yoked with excellent tawny steeds, drove straight toward Bhīṣma's car.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadavicitreṇa karṇikāreṇa ketunā abhyavarṣata bhīṣmaṃ ca tāṃś caiva rathasattamān
english: With his banner of the karṇikāra blossom, bright with gold, he rained his shafts upon Bhīṣma and upon those foremost of car-warriors.

sanskrit: sa tālaketos tīkṣṇena ketum āhatya patriṇā bhīṣmeṇa yuyudhe vīras tasya cānucaraiḥ saha
english: Striking the banner of him whose ensign was the palmyra with a keen, feathered shaft, that hero did battle with Bhīṣma and with his followers.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmāṇam ekena śalyaṃ pañcabhir āyasaiḥ viddhvā navabhir ānarchac chitāgraiḥ prapitāmaham
english: Having pierced Kṛtavarman with one iron shaft and Śalya with five, he struck the great-grandsire with nine keen-pointed arrows.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena samyak praṇihitena ca dhvajam ekena vivyādha jāmbūnadavibhūṣitam
english: With a single arrow, loosed from a fully drawn bow and well aimed, he pierced the gold-adorned banner.

sanskrit: durmukhasya tu bhallena sarvāvaraṇabhedinā jahāra sāratheḥ kāyāc chiraḥ saṃnataparvaṇā
english: And with a broad-headed, smooth-jointed shaft that cleaves through every guard, he struck the head of Durmukha's charioteer from his body.

sanskrit: dhanuś ciccheda bhallena kārtasvaravibhūṣitam kṛpasya niśitāgreṇa tāṃś ca tīkṣṇamukhaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: With a keen-pointed broad-headed shaft he cut apart the gold-adorned bow of Kṛpa, and assailed those warriors with sharp-mouthed arrows.

sanskrit: jaghāna paramakruddho nṛtyann iva mahārathaḥ tasya lāghavam udvīkṣya tutuṣur devatā api
english: In utmost fury that great car-warrior smote them, seeming to dance; and beholding his deftness, even the gods were delighted.

sanskrit: labdhalakṣyatayā karṣṇeḥ sarve bhīṣmamukhā rathāḥ sattvavantam amanyanta sākṣād iva dhanaṃjayam
english: By the unerring aim of the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, all the car-warriors led by Bhīṣma deemed him a man of valor, Dhanaṃjaya himself made manifest.

sanskrit: tasya lāghavamārgastham alātasadṛśaprabham diśaḥ paryapatac cāpaṃ gāṇḍīvam iva ghoṣavat
english: His bow, kept ever in the path of deftness, glowing like a firebrand, ranged about all the quarters, loud-voiced like the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: tam āsādya mahāvegair bhīṣmo navabhir āśugaiḥ vivyādha samare tūrṇam ārjuniṃ paravīrahā
english: Coming up against him, Bhīṣma, slayer of hostile heroes, swiftly pierced the son of Arjuna in battle with nine fast-flying arrows.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ cāsya tribhir bhallaiś ciccheda paramaujasaḥ sārathiṃ ca tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna yatavrataḥ
english: And with three broad-headed shafts he cut down the banner of that one of surpassing might, and that man of steadfast vows struck his charioteer with three arrows.

sanskrit: tathaiva kṛtavarmā ca kṛpaḥ śalyaś ca māriṣa viddhvā nākampayat kārṣṇiṃ mainākam iva parvatam
english: In like manner Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, and Śalya, O honored sir, though they pierced the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, could not make him waver, like the mountain Maināka.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūro dhārtarāṣṭrair mahārathaiḥ vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi kārṣṇiḥ pañcarathān prati
english: Surrounded by those great car-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's side, that hero, the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, poured showers of arrows upon the five chariot-fighters.

sanskrit: tatas teṣāṃ mahāstrāṇi saṃvārya śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ nanāda balavān kārṣṇir bhīṣmāya visṛjañ śarān
english: Then, warding off their great missiles with showers of arrows, the mighty son of Kṛṣṇa's sister roared aloud, loosing his shafts against Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tatrāsya sumahad rājan bāhvor balam adṛśyata yatamānasya samare bhīṣmam ardayataḥ śaraiḥ
english: There, O king, the exceeding strength of his arms was made plain as he strove in battle and harried Bhīṣma with his arrows.

sanskrit: parākrāntasya tasyaiva bhīṣmo 'pi prāhiṇoc charān sa tāṃś ciccheda samare bhīṣmacāpacyutāñ śarān
english: Against that very valiant one Bhīṣma too sent forth his shafts; but he cut to pieces in battle those arrows loosed from Bhīṣma's bow.

sanskrit: tato dhvajam amogheṣur bhīṣmasya navabhiḥ śaraiḥ ciccheda samare vīras tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: Then that hero of unfailing aim cut down Bhīṣma's banner in battle with nine arrows, and thereupon the people shouted aloud.

sanskrit: sa rājato mahāskandhas tālo hemavibhūṣitaḥ saubhadraviśikhaiś chinnaḥ papāta bhuvi bhārata
english: That silver palmyra of mighty stem, adorned with gold, cut down by the shafts of Subhadrā's son, fell to the earth, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhvajaṃ saubhadraviśikhaiḥ patitaṃ bharatarṣabha dṛṣṭvā bhīmo 'nadad dhṛṣṭaḥ saubhadram abhiharṣayan
english: Seeing the banner fallen by the arrows of Subhadrā's son, O bull of the Bhāratas, Bhīma roared in delight, gladdening the heart of Subhadrā's son.

sanskrit: atha bhīṣmo mahāstrāṇi divyāni ca bahūni ca prāduścakre mahāraudraḥ kṣaṇe tasmin mahābalaḥ
english: Then Bhīṣma, of fearful aspect and great strength, brought forth in that moment many mighty and celestial missiles.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasreṇa saubhadraṃ prapitāmahaḥ avākirad ameyātmā śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: Then the great-grandsire of immeasurable spirit overwhelmed the son of Subhadrā with a hundred thousand smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tato daśa maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ rakṣārtham abhyadhāvanta saubhadraṃ tvaritā rathaiḥ
english: Then ten great bowmen, mighty car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, sped forward upon their chariots to protect the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: virāṭaḥ saha putreṇa dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ bhīmaś ca kekayāś caiva sātyakiś ca viśāṃ pate
english: Virāṭa with his son, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata, and Bhīma, and the Kekayas, and Sātyaki, O lord of the peoples—

sanskrit: javenāpatatāṃ teṣāṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo raṇe pāñcālyaṃ tribhir ānarchat sātyakiṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As these swept down in haste, Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu, in battle, struck the Pāñcāla prince with three arrows and Sātyaki with sharp ones.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena kṣureṇa niśitena ca dhvajam ekena ciccheda bhīmasenasya patriṇā
english: And with a single keen, razor-edged, feathered shaft, loosed from a fully drawn bow, he cut down the banner of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayaḥ ketuḥ kesarī narasattama papāta bhīmasenasya bhīṣmeṇa mathito rathāt
english: The golden banner of Bhīmasena, bearing a lion, O best of men, struck down by Bhīṣma, fell from his chariot.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tribhir viddhvā bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ raṇe kṛpam ekena vivyādha kṛtavarmāṇam aṣṭabhiḥ
english: Bhīmasena, having pierced Bhīṣma the son of Śaṃtanu with three arrows in battle, struck Kṛpa with one and Kṛtavarman with eight.

sanskrit: pragṛhītāgrahastena vairāṭir api dantinā abhyadravata rājānaṃ madrādhipatim uttaraḥ
english: And Uttara, the son of Virāṭa, mounted upon an elephant whose trunk was raised on high, rushed against the king, the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: tasya vāraṇarājasya javenāpatato rathī śalyo nivārayām āsa vegam apratimaṃ raṇe
english: As that royal elephant came rushing down in haste, the charioteer Śalya checked its matchless onset in the battle.
